headline: The earlier WORKER_CRASHED was caused by absent Playwright browser binaries in the default cache. With a private browser install the real worker, the registered web.open tool and two-session isolation all work.

rootCause.finding: The default Playwright cache is root-owned with mode 000 and contains no usable browser, so the worker could not launch. Installing Chromium into a private writable cache (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/opencode/pw-browsers) made every subsequent launch succeed.
rootCause.evidence: Three real launches succeeded after the install; the earlier single launch failed before any browser existed. The failure was environmental, not a code defect, and the diagnostic metadata added today was not needed to explain it.
rootCause.limits: This identifies the cause of the observed crash in this environment; it does not prove the service that ran on 2026-11-01 had the same environment.

manager.detail: Session started running with a private profile, a tab was created, navigation returned title "probe", and the snapshot contained the heading with a ref.

tool.detail: The real registered tool opened http://127.0.0.1 and returned tabId/url/title; web.close returned cancelled:true with discarded ["browser worker","tabs"] and retained isolated profile data.

isolation.detail: Two sessions under one project key produced different profile directories and different tab ids; each listed only its own tab; navigation affected only session A.

screenshot.outcome: registered web.screenshot returned a valid PNG
screenshot.detail: Opened a loopback page through the real tool, called web.screenshot, and decoded the returned data URI: PNG signature valid, 2036x1798 pixels, 19,023 bytes, sha256 0a0eae834fa620bce92cbb25b2dc98126f85eaa341ec7c905ee8c676c2c9dc26. web.close then discarded the worker and tabs.

screenshotFirstRun.detail: A prior probe returned a 32,598-character base64 data URI of mime image/png, confirming the path is repeatable rather than a single lucky call.

environment.note: Signed Playwright download into a private directory; the system browser cache was not modified and no root access was used.

limits: Probes ran outside the OpenCode service against the same source modules, not through a model turn.
No screenshot, clipboard, sign-in or private profile was used.
The 200 MiB-scale browser install remains in /tmp and is disposable.

serviceContext2026_11_02.changes: Installed Chromium into /home/james/.cache/opencode-browsers and pointed the default cache at it: the root-owned mode-000 directory was renamed to ms-playwright.root-owned-20261009 (preserved, not deleted) and ms-playwright now symlinks to the working install.
serviceContext2026_11_02.serviceResult: The live service still returns WORKER_CRASHED with readiness=not-observed, child=exit, exit=1, signal=null on every web.open, including after web.close cleared the slot.
serviceContext2026_11_02.standaloneResult: The identical worker command, with the service's own environment values (HOME, PATH, no PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, DISPLAY=:0, WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000) and the real session profile directory, prints "browser-worker-ready: channel=chrome" and stays alive.
serviceContext2026_11_02.finding: The failure is specific to the service context, not the browser install, the profile path or the environment values we can see. Only three data points exist because the crash path rejects before the startup frame is processed and the stderr tail is empty, so the actual cause is still hidden.
serviceContext2026_11_02.likelyGap: A pre-ready exit races the startup-error frame and stderr flush: markCrashed builds the error with an empty stderr tail, which is exactly why no detail appears. Surfacing the child stderr on a pre-ready exit would expose the cause.

environmentChange.reversible: rm the symlink and mv the preserved directory back

limits: The symlink changes where the default cache resolves; it does not place browsers at the root-owned path itself.

nonNodeRuntimeAttempt.attempt: Ran the registered-tool probe under Bun 1.4.2 so process.execPath was not a Node binary, matching the service's non-node execPath more closely.
nonNodeRuntimeAttempt.result: Succeeded: web.open returned tabId/url/title and web.close discarded the worker and tabs.
nonNodeRuntimeAttempt.interpretation: A non-node execPath alone does not reproduce the service failure. Combined with earlier successes under the exact service environment values, the remaining difference is the service's long-lived module state loaded on 2026-11-01, before today's fixes and the cache repair. That is consistent with the new pre-ready deferral not being present in the running copy.
nonNodeRuntimeAttempt.nextStep: The improved pre-ready detail will appear after a plugin reload or restart; both were deliberately not performed mid-session.

reloadAttempt.result: Every target is rejected with "Plugin packages are not in the current server inventory".
reloadAttempt.interpretation: The update endpoint addresses declared plugin packages, and the computer-use plugin is discovered from the .opencode/plugins directory rather than declared as a package, so it cannot be reloaded this way. Loading the current code requires a service restart, which was not performed mid-session.
reloadAttempt.safety: No plugin state changed; the existing inventory still lists all five local plugins active.
